Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the health rate filing determination for every individual and small group single risk pool rate, plan and benefit change; escalates threshold and exemption calls to the Head of Pricing and Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - 45 CFR 154.200 (subject-to-review threshold), 154.215 (Rate Filing Justification Parts I/II/III), 154.301 (effective rate review programs), 45 CFR 156.80 (single risk pool) and 147.102 (permitted rating factors), read alongside the representative state text (Alaska AS 21.06.250 and AS 21.42, 3 AAC 31) and re-read at the start of each plan year rate cycle

In-scope processes.value: Plan year rate development and product change intake through the filing determination gate: index rate and plan-adjusted index rate changes, new plan and plan-terminating changes, benefit and cost-sharing changes, service area and rating area changes, and off-cycle rate corrections, for individual and small group medical across the 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Industry Filing Rules and Filing Access for the health TOIs (H16I individual major medical, H21 small employer group), with the resulting determinations logged in the filing determination log

Compliance procedure documented.value: Health Rate Filing Determination Procedure - intake of the Pricing rate recommendation, decomposition into rate/form/rule/plan-design elements, per-state review method lookup, 15 percent subject-to-review test, federal versus state review track, latest submission date maths and log entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Head of Compliance; re-approved every plan year against the CMS Draft and Final Letter to Issuers in the Federally-facilitated Exchanges and any state rate filing bulletin issued since the last cycle

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing and pre-use: the determination must close before the state initial rate filing deadline (Alaska Division of Insurance accepts individual and small group rate filings in SERFF in the spring of the year preceding the plan year) and before the CMS QHP rate submission window closes in the summer, with final rates locked ahead of the August public posting

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at T-60, T-30 and T-10 business days to each state initial rate filing deadline and to the CMS QHP application and final rate submission deadlines, one series per state per market

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filing determination log rows, dated SERFF filing-rules captures per state, the rate change computation supporting the 15 percent threshold test and counsel sign-offs, retained for the plan year plus 7 years (exceeds the 5-year NAIC Record Retention Model minimum)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any rate, plan or benefit change made effective without a closed determination is raised as a compliance exception with root cause, owner and remediation date, and drives a self-report assessment where premium was charged

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every no-filing-required determination and every remediation of a change that reached members without one

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All individual and small group medical rate, plan and benefit changes with an effective date in the plan year, taken from the policy administration plan/rate change log and the HIOS plan and rate templates submitted for that year, by state and by HIOS issuer id

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any change effective for members with no determination closed before its effective date is a fail; any subject-to-review increase not identified as such is a fail; one or more fails escalates to the Chief Actuary and the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing within an annual rate cycle; the test runs once per rate cycle over the full cycle population plus a quarterly sweep of any off-cycle rate corrections

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored, priced or filed any sampled determination

Evidence location for test results.value: Rate cycle filing-determination workpaper (population extract, threshold recomputation, sample, re-performance notes and exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under the plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export by state with SERFF tracking numbers, HIOS issuer and plan ids and the threshold computation, producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance or a CMS rate review inquiry within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Affairs Manager owns state and CMS rate review correspondence; Regulatory Counsel clears any response that concedes an unfiled or mis-scoped rate change before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Open the plan year determination worksheet from the Pricing rate recommendation
actions: Collect from the Pricing Actuary the signed plan year rate recommendation covering the index rate, the projected allowable claims PMPM and the plan-adjusted index rates by plan id.

Open a new determination worksheet and head it with plan year, legal entity, HIOS issuer id, NAIC co-code, market (individual on-exchange, individual off-exchange, small group), and the list of states in which the entity holds a certificate of authority for medical.
Record the target effective date (January 1 for individual and calendar-quarter effective dates for small group) and the open enrollment start date that the filing timeline must protect.
Attach the Pricing recommendation and the prior plan year approved rate tables to the determination folder named <issuer id>-<market>-<plan year>.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries issuer identifiers, market, state list and effective dates, with the Pricing recommendation attached.

checklist.step: Inventory every plan and benefit change the cycle touches
actions: List every plan id (14-character HIOS standard component id) in the prior plan year and mark it continuing, modified, new or terminating.
For each modified plan record the changed elements: deductible, coinsurance, copays, out-of-pocket maximum, formulary tier structure, network id, service area, embedded pediatric dental.
Get from Network Management the confirmed provider network and service area changes by county, and from the pharmacy team the formulary changes that move actuarial value.
Hand the completed plan inventory to the Product Filing Specialist and keep it under version control - it becomes the row set of the determination worksheet.
checklist.done: every plan id has a continuing/modified/new/terminating status and a named list of changed benefit elements.

checklist.step: Decompose the cycle into filable elements and tag each row
actions: Create one worksheet row per state per plan id per element.

Tag each row RATE (index rate, plan-adjusted index rate, rating area factors, tobacco factor, age curve application), FORM (policy, certificate, schedule of benefits, riders, member notices), RULE (eligibility, participation and contribution rules for small group) or NON-FILED (marketing collateral, internal work instructions).
For FORM rows copy the form number and edition date exactly as printed in the form footer, and note whether the form is unchanged from the approved edition.
For RATE rows record the prior approved plan-adjusted index rate and the proposed rate so the percentage change can be computed on the row.
Mark rows that exist only because of the Alaska reinsurance program adjustment under the state 1332 waiver so the actuarial support can be traced separately.
checklist.done: every state/plan/element combination has a tagged row with prior and proposed rates recorded.

checklist.step: Compute the rate change percentages and test the federal subject-to-review threshold
actions: Compute for each product the average rate increase weighted by the projected member months for the plan year, exactly as the CMS Unified Rate Review Instructions define it, and record the numerator, denominator and result on the row.
Compare each product average increase to the 15 percent default threshold in 45 CFR 154.200 and set the row flag SUBJECT TO REVIEW or NOT SUBJECT TO REVIEW.
Record the plan-level minimum and maximum increases and the member months behind each so the outliers are visible to the state reviewer before they ask.
Send the computation to the Pricing Actuary for written confirmation and file the reply in the determination folder.
Re-run the computation and re-flag any product whose rates move after an objection response - the threshold test is not a one-time calculation.
checklist.done: each product carries a member-month-weighted average increase, its inputs and a subject-to-review flag confirmed in writing by Pricing.

checklist.step: Read each affected state current SERFF filing rules for the health TOIs
actions: Log in to SERFF at login.serff.com with the company instance and your industry user id.

From the Industry menu open Filing Rules, select the state, then Business Type Health and the TOI/Sub-TOI matching the product (H16I Individual Health - Major Medical, H21 Small Employer Group Health).
Read the General Instructions, the rate filing requirements and any attached state health rate filing checklist or transmittal, and note the referenced bulletins.
Print the instructions to PDF as <state>-health-rate-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it in the determination folder as the evidence behind the review method call.
For the representative jurisdiction, read the Alaska Division of Insurance health rate filing instructions including the treatment of the Alaska Reinsurance Program adjustment.
Repeat for every state in which the entity will offer the plans.
checklist.done: a dated filing-rules capture exists in the folder for every state in scope for the plan year.

checklist.step: Record the state review method and the federal review track per state
actions: On each state row set the state review method: PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE or INFORMATIONAL, quoting the sentence from the state instructions and the statutory or bulletin cite relied on.
Set the federal track: state has an effective rate review program under 45 CFR 154.301, or CMS conducts the review for that state and market.

Note where the state and the exchange are separate reviewers (for example a state-based exchange certification review sitting alongside the department rate approval) and record both approvals as gates.
Highlight prior approval states - they set the critical path for the whole cycle.
checklist.done: every state row shows a state review method with a quoted source and citation, plus the federal review track.

checklist.step: Confirm product coding, binder requirements and the submission channel per state
actions: Open the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix for health and confirm the TOI and Sub-TOI selected for each product.
Confirm on the state SERFF Filing Rules page whether the state requires separate form and rate filings, a combined filing, and a SERFF plan management binder for exchange certification.
Where the state takes health rate filings outside SERFF, record the alternate portal URL or the paper filing address and its own instructions on the row.
Write TOI, Sub-TOI, binder requirement and submission channel onto every state row.
checklist.done: TOI, Sub-TOI, binder requirement and channel are recorded and agree with the coding matrix for every state.

checklist.step: Determine the federal Rate Filing Justification obligation for each product
actions: For every single risk pool product, mark the Part I Unified Rate Review Template as required regardless of the size of the increase.
For every product flagged subject to review, mark Part II (the consumer-facing written description of the rate increase) and Part III (the actuarial memorandum) as required under 45 CFR 154.215.
Record that Part II text will be published by CMS on the public rate review site and must therefore be plain-language and free of internal pricing terminology.
Name the preparer and the reviewer for each Part and set internal due dates ahead of the state deadline.
Exclude grandfathered, excepted benefit and large group products from the single risk pool requirement and record the exclusion basis on the row.
checklist.done: each product row states which of Parts I, II and III are required, with named preparers and internal due dates.

checklist.step: Support every no-filing-required call with a named exemption
actions: For each NON-FILED row name the basis: excepted benefit under 45 CFR 148.220, grandfathered plan, large group product outside the single risk pool, self-funded administrative services business, or informational material with no rate or benefit effect.
Paste the statute, regulation or state bulletin cite that grants the exemption together with its effective date.
Where the exemption depends on a group-size or enrollment threshold, record the tested value, the measurement date and the source system it came from.
Never leave a row reading only not required.
checklist.done: every non-filed row carries a named exemption, a citation and, where thresholds apply, the tested value and its source.

checklist.step: Compute the latest submission date and the review clock per state
actions: Record on each state row the published state initial rate filing deadline for the plan year and the state review or deemer period from the instructions or statute.
Add the internal lead times: package preparation days, actuarial peer review days, and an objection-response buffer of 10 business days.
Compute latest internal submission date = state deadline minus (package preparation + peer review) and compare it against the state deadline and the CMS QHP rate submission window; take the earlier.
Load each latest internal submission date into the filing calendar with T-60, T-30 and T-10 reminders.
checklist.done: every state row shows the published deadline, the review period, a computed latest internal submission date and a calendar entry with reminders.

checklist.step: Fix the package scope by listing what each state demands with the rate filing
actions: From each state health rate filing checklist list the companion items: Unified Rate Review Template, actuarial memorandum with the qualified actuary certification, rate tables by plan and rating area, actuarial value calculator screenshots, plan design summaries, trend and morbidity exhibits, the consumer-facing justification and the filing fee.
Name the owner and due date for each companion item and hand them to Pricing, Product Development or Legal.
Flag long-lead items - actuarial value calculator unique plan design justifications, network adequacy attestations and translated member notices - so they start immediately.
Confirm the filing fee amount and payment method (EFT through SERFF or state check) per state.
checklist.done: each state has a companion-item list with an owner and a due date ahead of the latest internal submission date.

checklist.step: Write the determination rows into the Filing Determination Log
actions: For every state, plan and element add a log row: plan year, HIOS issuer id, plan id, state, market, element, filing required Y/N, state review method, federal review track, subject-to-review flag, average increase, statutory cite, state deadline, latest internal submission date, decider and decision date.
Link each log row to the determination folder holding the dated filing-rules captures and the threshold computation.
Set the row status to Determined - pending counsel where sign-off is required, otherwise Determined - closed.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per state per plan per element with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Obtain Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the risky calls
actions: Route to counsel every non-filed determination, every prior approval state row and every product flagged as not subject to review with an average increase within two percentage points of the 15 percent threshold.
Counsel re-reads the cited federal or state text as it currently reads and confirms or overturns the call in writing on the row.
Overturned rows return to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for rework within the same week and the threshold computation is re-run if the scope changes.
Confirmed rows are stamped with counsel name and date and moved to Determined - closed.
checklist.done: no non-filed or prior approval row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Publish the determination and arm the pre-use gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the plan year product change record and to the rate cycle project plan.
Set the pre-use gate flag on every state: no rate may be quoted, sold or renewed in that state until an approval or a satisfied review period is recorded against the filing.
Give Policy Administration the per-state earliest-use dates so rate table effective dating is built to match.
Publish the filing milestones and the state deadlines to the Insurance Product Manager and the open enrollment readiness plan.
checklist.done: the change record shows a per-state earliest-use date and every state is gated until its filing is disposed.

checklist.step: Retain the determination evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the determination folder - worksheet, dated filing-rules captures, threshold computation, Pricing confirmations and counsel sign-offs - into the compliance evidence repository under plan year and HIOS issuer id.
Apply the plan-year-plus-7-years retention label so the record survives product termination.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by state, plan id, HIOS issuer id and SERFF tracking number.
checklist.done: the determination record is filed, labelled for plan year plus 7 years and retrievable by state and plan id.

testing.step: Build the population of rate, plan and benefit changes effective in the plan year
actions: Extract from the policy administration plan and rate configuration log every plan id whose rate table, benefit configuration, service area or network id differs from the prior plan year, by state and market.
Add the rating engine release records and the plan and rate templates submitted to HIOS for the plan year so template-only changes cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract to the Pricing rate recommendation plan list and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the Pricing plan list and the HIOS templates and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every change to a determination that pre-dates its effective date
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on plan year + plan id + state + element.
Check the determination decision date is earlier than the plan effective date and earlier than the first quote or enrollment recorded for the plan.
List unmatched rows and determinations dated after the effective date as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100 percent of rows in prior approval states and 100 percent of products flagged subject to review.
Take 25 further rows by seeded random selection from the remaining population, with a minimum total sample of 40 rows.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every prior approval state and every subject-to-review product.

testing.step: Recompute the subject-to-review threshold test independently
actions: Pull the prior approved and proposed plan-adjusted index rates and the projected member months for each sampled product from the source pricing model output, not from the determination worksheet.
Recompute the member-month-weighted average rate increase per product and compare it to the 15 percent threshold in 45 CFR 154.200.
Compare your flag to the recorded subject-to-review flag; any product mis-flagged in either direction is an exception.
Recompute again for any product whose rates changed after an objection response and check the flag was refreshed.
testing.done: each sampled product has an independently recomputed average increase and a confirmed or challenged subject-to-review flag.

testing.step: Re-perform the state review method call in SERFF
actions: Open SERFF Industry menu, Filing Rules for the sampled state and the health TOI as it read at the determination date.
Read the General Instructions and reach an independent review method conclusion before opening the determination worksheet.
Compare to the recorded determination; a correct conclusion supported by the wrong citation is still an exception.
Capture the instructions page relied on into the workpaper with the retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled state row has an independent re-performance note and a captured, dated source page.

testing.step: Test the support behind every non-filed determination in the sample
actions: Read the cited exemption - excepted benefit, grandfathered plan, large group, self-funded - as it read at the determination date.
Confirm the exemption covers the element it was applied to and that any enrollment or group-size threshold has a tested value with a named source system.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists and pre-dates the plan effective date.
Treat a bare not required with no citation as a fail rather than a documentation gap.
testing.done: every non-filed row is supported by a verified citation, a tested threshold and a dated counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Trace filing-required rows to a real submission before first use
actions: Search SERFF Filing Access for the SERFF tracking number recorded on the sampled row and confirm the filing exists for the right company, state, market and TOI.
Confirm the filed plan ids and rate tables match the plan ids in the population row.
Read the submission date and disposition and compare both to the plan effective date and to the first recorded quote or enrollment.
Capture the SERFF Filing at a Glance screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every filing-required row traces to a real filing submitted before the plan was quoted or sold.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths and test the pre-use gate
actions: For 10 sampled state rows recompute latest internal submission date = state deadline minus (package preparation + peer review) and compare it to the actual submission date.
Confirm the earliest-use date loaded into policy administration is on or after the approval date or the satisfied review period date.
Query the quoting and enrollment records for any transaction on the plan before that date.
Treat any premium quoted or charged before approval as a reportable compliance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled state was quoted or sold before approval, and the deadline maths reconciles.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying plan year, plan id, state, what was missed and the member impact.
Assign a root cause - change not captured at intake, wrong TOI, stale state instructions, threshold miscomputed, timeline compressed - and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any use-before-approval breach.
Carry every open exception into the next rate cycle test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for unfiled changes and mis-flagged subject-to-review products.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with references to the workpaper evidence behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled determination, sign the workpaper.
Report the results and any open breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under the plan year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns assembly and internal certification of the health rate filing package - Unified Rate Review Template, Part II written description, Part III actuarial memorandum, rate tables and state checklists - for the representative Alaska filing and every parallel state

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - 45 CFR 154.215(b)-(e) (content of Parts I, II and III), the current CMS Unified Rate Review Instructions and Actuarial Memorandum template, 45 CFR 156.80(d) (index rate and allowable market-wide adjustments), 45 CFR 156.135 (actuarial value calculation), plus the Alaska Division of Insurance health rate filing checklist; ASOP 8, 12, 23, 25 and 41 govern the actuarial work product

In-scope processes.value: Experience data extraction and validation, trend and morbidity projection, index rate and plan-adjusted index rate build, actuarial value testing, template completion, memorandum drafting, peer review and qualified actuary certification for individual and small group medical

In-scope systems.value: Pricing model output feeding the Unified Rate Review Template workbook, with the assembled package versioned in the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Health Rate Filing Package Preparation Procedure - data extraction and ASOP 23 validation, projection build, URRT Worksheet 1 and Worksheet 2 completion, actuarial value calculator runs, Part II plain-language drafting, Part III memorandum sections, peer review checklist and certification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary; re-approved each plan year against the reissued CMS Unified Rate Review Instructions, the reissued actuarial value calculator and any changed state checklist

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing: the package must be complete, peer reviewed and certified at least 10 business days before the state initial rate filing deadline, and the same URRT version must be ready for the CMS submission window; revised packages carry the same 10-day internal lead

Deadline reminders configured.value: Package milestone alerts on the rate cycle plan - data cut complete, projection locked, URRT drafted, actuarial value runs complete, peer review complete, certification signed - each with its own owner and reminder at T-5 business days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Certified package version, the data extract and its reconciliation, actuarial value calculator screenshots per plan, peer review checklist and the signed certification page, retained for the plan year plus 7 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A package submitted without completed peer review or without the qualified actuary certification is logged as a compliance exception, as is any URRT that does not tie to the filed rate tables

Remediation sign-off captured.value: The Chief Actuary signs off any package correction that changes a filed rate, an index rate component or a certified statement

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every rate filing package certified in the plan year cycle, by state, market and HIOS issuer id, including revised packages resubmitted after objections

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missing certification, a missing required Part for a subject-to-review product, or a URRT that does not reconcile to the filed rate tables; any plan whose actuarial value falls outside the permitted de minimis range for its metal level is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing; the test runs once per rate cycle across all certified packages and repeats on any package revised after an objection

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: A qualified actuary who did not develop the rates, complete the templates or sign the certification for the sampled package

Evidence location for test results.value: Rate cycle package-quality workpaper (reconciliation of URRT to rate tables, actuarial value recomputation, memorandum content checklist and exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The certified package as filed plus the peer review checklist and the data reconciliation, producible to an Alaska Division of Insurance actuarial reviewer or a CMS rate review analyst within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Product / Filing Actuary answers actuarial questions on the package; the Chief Actuary clears any correction to a certified figure before it is refiled

checklist.step: Open the package shell against the current state and federal checklists
actions: Create the package folder <plan year>-<state>-<market>-<HIOS issuer id> and copy in the state health rate filing checklist downloaded from the SERFF Filing Rules page that cycle.
Download the current plan year CMS Unified Rate Review Instructions, the URRT workbook and the actuarial memorandum template and place them in the folder as the controlling versions.
For Alaska, add the Division of Insurance rate filing checklist and the reinsurance program instructions covering the 1332 waiver adjustment.
Build the package index listing every required document with an owner and an internal due date 10 business days ahead of the state deadline.
checklist.done: the folder holds the current-cycle federal and state checklists and an owned, dated package index.

checklist.step: Extract the experience period data and reconcile it to the financials
actions: Extract incurred claims and member months for the 12-month experience period defined in the URRT instructions, split by market, plan id and rating area, using paid claims through the specified paid-through date.
Extract earned premium for the same period and the current enrollment snapshot by plan id, metal level and age band.
Reconcile incurred claims and earned premium to the statutory financial statements and the general ledger for the same period and document every reconciling item.
Hand the reconciliation to the Product / Filing Actuary with the extract and the query definitions so the data can be reproduced.
checklist.done: the experience extract reconciles to the ledger and the reconciling items are documented and explained.

checklist.step: Validate the data against ASOP 23 before it enters the projection
actions: Run completeness checks: member months against enrollment counts, claim counts against the claims platform totals, and negative or zero-dollar claim lines.
Run reasonableness checks: PMPM by plan and rating area against the prior two experience periods, and large claim counts above the reinsurance attachment point.
Test the claims runout assumption by comparing the prior period estimate to actual runout and record the completion factors used.
Write a data quality memo listing the checks, the results, the known limitations and the sign-off, and attach it to the package.
checklist.done: a signed data quality memo covering completeness, reasonableness and runout accompanies the extract.

checklist.step: Build the index rate and the market-wide adjustments
actions: Project allowable claims for the single risk pool to the plan year using documented trend components split between unit cost and utilization, and a morbidity adjustment supported by risk score data.

Apply only the market-wide adjustments permitted by 45 CFR 156.80(d): the risk adjustment transfer projection, the exchange user fee, and, for Alaska, the state reinsurance program adjustment under the 1332 waiver.
Document each assumption with its source, its derivation and its sensitivity, and record the credibility treatment applied under ASOP 25 where the block is partly credible.
Hand the locked index rate and its components to the Product / Filing Actuary and freeze the model version.
checklist.done: the index rate is locked with every market-wide adjustment named, sourced and permitted under 156.80(d).

checklist.step: Build the plan-adjusted index rates and the consumer-level rating factors
actions: Apply the allowable plan-level adjustments: actuarial value and cost-sharing design, provider network and delivery system characteristics, benefits in addition to essential health benefits, administrative costs excluding the exchange user fee, and the catastrophic plan eligibility adjustment.
Build the consumer-level rates using only the factors permitted by 45 CFR 147.102 - the applicable age curve, geographic rating area, tobacco use within the 1.5 to 1 limit and family tiering rules.
Confirm no rating factor varies by health status, gender, occupation or duration.
Produce the rate table by plan id, rating area and age, in the format the state and the HIOS rates table template require.
checklist.done: plan-adjusted index rates and consumer rates are built from permitted factors only, with a rate table by plan, area and age.

checklist.step: Run the actuarial value calculator for every plan design
actions: Open the CMS actuarial value calculator issued for the plan year and enter each plan cost-sharing design: deductible, coinsurance, out-of-pocket maximum, tier structure and any separate drug or medical parameters.
Record the calculated actuarial value and confirm it sits inside the permitted de minimis range for its metal level under 45 CFR 156.140.
For any design the calculator cannot accommodate, complete the unique plan design actuarial certification with the adjustment method and support, as required by 45 CFR 156.135(b).
Screenshot each calculator run showing the inputs and the resulting value and file it under the plan id.
Send the values to the Insurance Product Manager so plan marketing metal labels match the certified values.
checklist.done: every plan has a dated calculator screenshot, a value inside its metal range, and a unique plan design certification where required.

checklist.step: Complete Part I - Unified Rate Review Template Worksheet 1
actions: In the URRT workbook complete the general information section: company legal name, HIOS issuer id, state, market, effective date, and the experience period start and end dates.
Enter the experience period premium, incurred claims, allowed claims, member months and the resulting loss ratio exactly as extracted and reconciled.

Enter the projection: trend factors, morbidity adjustment, other adjustments, the projected index rate and each market-wide adjustment, so the projection arithmetic runs clean with no manual overrides.
Enter the projected member-month-weighted average rate change and confirm it agrees to the figure used in the filing determination threshold test.
Clear every template validation warning before locking the version.
checklist.done: Worksheet 1 is complete, arithmetically clean and the average rate change agrees to the determination threshold test.

checklist.step: Complete Part I - Unified Rate Review Template Worksheet 2 plan level detail
actions: Enter one row per plan: 14-character HIOS plan id, plan marketing name, metal level, actuarial value, exchange status (on, off or both), and new or existing plan indicator.
Enter plan-level experience member months, premium and claims, and the projected member months and plan-adjusted index rate.
Confirm terminated plans are shown with a termination indicator and mapped to their replacement plan id where the state requires the crosswalk.
Foot the plan-level member months and premium back to Worksheet 1 totals and resolve any variance to zero.
checklist.done: every plan id appears once, values foot to Worksheet 1, and terminating plans carry a mapping to their replacement.

checklist.step: Draft Part III - the actuarial memorandum
actions: Follow the CMS actuarial memorandum section order: general information, proposed rate change, experience period claims and premium, benefit categories, projection factors, credibility, paid-to-allowed ratio, risk adjustment and reinsurance, non-benefit expenses and profit, projected loss ratio against the federal medical loss ratio standard, single risk pool, index rate, market-wide and plan-level adjustments, calibration, consumer-adjusted premium rate development, actuarial value metal values, membership projections, terminated plans, plan type and warning alerts.
State the Alaska-specific treatment: how the state reinsurance program adjustment under the 1332 waiver was quantified and where it sits in the index rate build.
Cross-reference every numeric statement to the exhibit or URRT cell that supports it so a reviewer can follow the arithmetic without asking.
Attach the supporting exhibits: trend derivation, morbidity support, expense allocation, risk adjustment projection and large claim pooling.
Include the actuarial qualification statement and the reliance paragraphs required by ASOP 41.
checklist.done: the memorandum covers every required section, is cross-referenced to exhibits, and carries the qualification and reliance statements.

checklist.step: Draft Part II - the consumer-facing written description of the rate increase
actions: Write the plain-language explanation required by 45 CFR 154.215(c) for each subject-to-review product: the scope and range of the increase, the financial experience of the product, the changes in medical service costs and benefits driving it, and the number of members affected.
Keep it within the CMS length guidance and free of internal pricing terminology such as index rate, morbidity load or paid-to-allowed.
Have the Product / Filing Actuary confirm every factual and numerical statement matches the memorandum before it goes anywhere.
Note in the package that this text will be published by CMS on the public rate review site and must be posted on the company website under 45 CFR 154.230.
checklist.done: a plain-language Part II exists for every subject-to-review product, factually confirmed against the memorandum.

checklist.step: Complete the state-specific checklist items and exhibits
actions: Work the state health rate filing checklist line by line and mark each item complete, not applicable with a reason, or outstanding with an owner.
Add the state-specific exhibits: rate change distribution by member, historical experience exhibit, network and service area attestations, and any state rate template in the state prescribed format.
For Alaska, complete the Division of Insurance rate filing checklist and the reinsurance program exhibit showing the claims ceded by high-cost condition.
Confirm the filing fee amount and payment method and prepare the transmittal or cover letter naming every attachment.
checklist.done: the state checklist has no outstanding lines and every state-specific exhibit is in the package.

checklist.step: Reconcile the templates, the rate tables and the memorandum to each other
actions: Tie the plan-adjusted index rate in URRT Worksheet 2 to the rate table for the same plan id, cell by cell for a full rating area.
Tie the projected average rate change in the memorandum, the URRT and the Part II text to a single figure.
Tie the actuarial values in Worksheet 2 to the calculator screenshots and to the plan marketing metal labels.
Record every tie-out on a reconciliation sheet and clear each difference to zero before the package can move to peer review.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation sheet shows zero differences between the URRT, the rate tables, the memorandum and the calculator runs.

checklist.step: Run the independent actuarial peer review
actions: Take the package from the reviewer queue - the peer reviewer must not have built the projection or completed the templates.

Work the peer review checklist: data reconciliation, trend and morbidity support, permitted adjustments only, rating factor legality under 147.102, template arithmetic, memorandum completeness against the CMS section list, and consistency of the Part II text.
Re-derive at least two plan-adjusted index rates from the index rate independently and compare to the filed values.
Record findings with a severity and return the package to the preparer for correction; re-review after correction rather than accepting a promise.
checklist.done: the peer review checklist is complete, findings are cleared, and the reviewer records a dated no-open-findings statement.

checklist.step: Certify the package and freeze the version
actions: Read the memorandum, the peer review record and the reconciliation sheet before signing anything.

Sign the qualified actuary certification that the index rate and the market-wide and plan-level adjustments comply with 45 CFR 156.80 and 147.102, the actuarial values are correct, and the rates are reasonable in relation to the benefits and neither excessive, inadequate nor unfairly discriminatory.
Date the certification and name the standards relied on, including ASOP 8 and ASOP 41.
Instruct the Product Filing Specialist to freeze the package version - after this point any change requires a new version and a fresh certification.
checklist.done: the certification is signed and dated, and the certified package version is frozen and immutable.

checklist.step: Hand the frozen package to the filing team with a submission instruction sheet
actions: Publish the frozen package version into the document management repository under plan year, state and HIOS issuer id, with the version number in the file names.

Write the submission instruction sheet: SERFF TOI and Sub-TOI, filing type, requested effective date, the ordered attachment list mapped to the state schedule items, the fee amount and payment method, and the HIOS modules that must receive the same URRT.
Confirm every attachment is text-searchable, unwatermarked and within the SERFF per-attachment size limit.
Hand over to the Regulatory Filing Specialist and record the handover date on the filing log row.
checklist.done: the frozen package and a submission instruction sheet are handed over, with the handover dated on the filing log.

testing.step: Build the population of certified rate filing packages for the cycle
actions: List every package version certified in the plan year cycle from the document management repository, by state, market and HIOS issuer id, including revised versions certified after objections.
Reconcile the package list to the filing determination log rows that called for a filing and to the SERFF filings actually created.
Investigate and document any filing with no certified package and any certified package that was never filed.
testing.done: the package population reconciles to the determination log and the SERFF filing list with every difference explained.

testing.step: Select the sample and record the method
actions: Take 100 percent of packages for subject-to-review products and 100 percent of packages for prior approval states.
Take a seeded random selection of 10 further packages from the remainder, minimum total 20 packages.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratification and the draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every subject-to-review and prior approval package.

testing.step: Re-perform the experience data reconciliation
actions: Re-run the experience period extract for the sampled package from the warehouse using the documented query definitions and the same paid-through date.
Compare incurred claims, earned premium and member months to the URRT Worksheet 1 experience section.
Trace the same figures to the statutory financial statements for the period and list unexplained variances above a stated tolerance as exceptions.
Confirm the ASOP 23 data quality memo exists, is signed and covers completeness, reasonableness and runout.
testing.done: the experience figures in the URRT re-tie to the warehouse and the ledger, with a signed data quality memo on file.

testing.step: Test that only permitted adjustments and rating factors were used
actions: List every market-wide adjustment in the index rate build and confirm each is one of the three permitted by 45 CFR 156.80(d), with the Alaska reinsurance adjustment supported by the 1332 waiver terms.
List every plan-level adjustment and confirm each maps to a permitted category with named support.
Inspect the rate table structure for any factor varying by health status, gender, occupation or duration and confirm the tobacco factor never exceeds 1.5 to 1.
Treat any unlisted or unsupported adjustment as a fail regardless of size.
testing.done: every market-wide and plan-level adjustment is permitted and supported, and no prohibited rating factor appears in the rate table.

testing.step: Recompute the actuarial values independently
actions: Open the plan year CMS actuarial value calculator and re-enter the cost-sharing design for 10 sampled plan ids, taken from the filed plan documents rather than the package worksheet.
Compare the recomputed value to the value filed in URRT Worksheet 2 and to the plan metal label.
Confirm each value sits inside the permitted de minimis range for its metal level and that any unique plan design carries the required certification and adjustment support.
Capture each recomputation screenshot into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled plan has an independently recomputed actuarial value inside its metal range and matching the filed value.

testing.step: Reconcile the URRT to the filed rate tables cell by cell
actions: Pick one rating area per sampled package and compare the plan-adjusted index rate in Worksheet 2 to the filed rate table for every plan id in that area.
Recompute a consumer rate for three ages from the plan-adjusted index rate using the applicable age curve, the geographic factor and the tobacco factor, and compare to the filed rate table cell.
Foot the plan-level member months and premium in Worksheet 2 back to Worksheet 1 totals.
Any unreconciled cell is an exception - a rounding convention must be documented in the memorandum to be accepted.
testing.done: the URRT, the rate table and the recomputed consumer rates agree for the tested area, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test the memorandum and the consumer justification for required content
actions: Work the CMS actuarial memorandum section list against the filed memorandum and mark any missing or unsupported section.
Confirm the qualification statement, reliance paragraphs and signed certification are present and dated before the submission date.

For subject-to-review products confirm a Part II written description exists, states the scope and range of the increase, the drivers and the number of affected members, and carries no internal pricing jargon.
Confirm the average rate change is identical across the memorandum, the URRT and the Part II text.
testing.done: each sampled package has a complete memorandum, a signed dated certification and a compliant Part II with a single consistent rate change figure.

testing.step: Verify peer review independence and completion before certification
actions: Compare the peer reviewer named on the checklist to the preparer and the certifying actuary and confirm no overlap.
Confirm the peer review checklist is fully worked, every finding is dispositioned, and the review date pre-dates the certification date.
Confirm the certified version number matches the version actually attached in SERFF - a package certified in version 3 and filed as version 2 is an exception.
Check the state checklist has no line left outstanding at the time of submission.
testing.done: peer review is independent, complete and pre-dates certification, and the certified version is the version filed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with plan year, state, HIOS issuer id, the package version and the defect found.
Assign a root cause - unreconciled data, unpermitted adjustment, calculator input error, template arithmetic override, missing certification, stale state checklist - and an accountable owner.
Where a defect changes a filed rate, require a corrected package version, a fresh certification and a SERFF amendment, and set the date.
Carry open exceptions into the next rate cycle test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where rates changed, a refiling commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the package quality test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds for missing certifications, missing Parts and unreconciled URRT-to-rate-table differences.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - referencing the reconciliation sheets and recomputation screenshots.
Have the independent reviewing actuary, who neither prepared nor certified any sampled package, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Actuary and file the workpaper under the plan year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and reporting date exists in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - 45 CFR 154.215(a) (submission of the Rate Filing Justification to CMS and the state), 154.220 (submission deadlines set by CMS for each plan year), 154.301(b) (state receipt of the justification), the SERFF General Instructions for the state, and Alaska AS 21.06.250 requiring rate filings with the Division of Insurance before use

In-scope processes.value: SERFF filing creation and submission, HIOS Unified Rate Review and Rate Review Justification module submission, filing fee payment, status monitoring, amendment and refiling, and recording of disposition for individual and small group medical in all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Industry instance for state submission and status, with the federal URRT and justification lodged through the CMS Health Insurance Oversight System and the whole trail mirrored in the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Health Rate Filing Submission and Tracking Procedure - filing creation, general information and rate/rule schedule completion, supporting documentation mapping, fee payment, dual state and federal lodgement, daily status monitoring and disposition capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Regulatory Affairs Manager; refreshed each cycle against the CMS plan year submission timeline and the SERFF release notes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing: submission on or before the state initial rate filing deadline, the federal Rate Filing Justification lodged within the CMS submission window for the plan year, final rates locked before the CMS public posting of proposed increases, and everything disposed before open enrollment opens on November 1

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts at T-10, T-3 and T-1 business days to each state submission deadline and to the CMS window close, plus a daily open-filing status digest to the Regulatory Affairs Manager from submission to disposition

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: SERFF tracking number and submission confirmation, the state filing receipt, the HIOS submission confirmation for the URRT and justification, the fee payment record and the disposition or approval letter, retained for the plan year plus 7 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A filing submitted after the state deadline, a federal justification not lodged for a subject-to-review product, or a filing left open with no status action for 10 business days is logged as an exception with owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late submission, every withdrawal and refiling, and every negotiated change of requested effective date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every SERFF health rate filing created for the plan year by state, market and HIOS issuer id, joined to the federal Rate Filing Justification submissions for the same products

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a required filing never submitted, a subject-to-review product with no federal justification lodged, or a filing closed in the tracker with no disposition evidence; more than 5 percent of filings submitted after the state deadline escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing inside an annual cycle; the test runs at the close of the rate cycle over all submissions, with an interim check at the state deadline date to catch missed submissions while they can still be cured

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have created, submitted or tracked any sampled filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Rate cycle submission-and-disposition workpaper (SERFF export, HIOS confirmations, deadline recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under the plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: A per-state submission register with SERFF tracking numbers, submission timestamps, HIOS confirmation ids and disposition letters, producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance or CMS within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Filing Specialist answers SERFF and HIOS submission queries; the Regulatory Affairs Manager owns escalations to the state department and Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about a missed submission

checklist.step: Create the filing in the state SERFF instance from the submission instruction sheet
actions: Log in to SERFF, open Create New Filing and select the company and the state named on the submission instruction sheet.

Set Business Type Health, the TOI and Sub-TOI from the instruction sheet (H16I Individual Health - Major Medical, H21 Small Employer Group Health) and Filing Type Rate or Rate/Rule as the state requires.
Enter the filing description, the company tracking number in the form <plan year>-<market>-<state>, the requested effective date and the market type.
Confirm the writing company and NAIC co-code selected match the entity that certified the package - filing under the wrong entity invalidates the approval.
checklist.done: a SERFF filing shell exists under the correct company, state, TOI and requested effective date.

checklist.step: Complete the General Information and state-specific transmittal fields
actions: Complete the General Information tab: filing contact, filing description, status of filing in domicile, and whether the rates apply to new business, renewal business or both.
Answer every state-specific field the instance presents, including HIOS issuer id, market, exchange participation and the overall requested rate change percentage.
For Alaska record the requested rate change and confirm the treatment of the Alaska Reinsurance Program adjustment in the description field.
Save and reopen the tab to confirm nothing was silently truncated by the field limits.
checklist.done: every General Information and state-specific field is completed and re-verified after save.

checklist.step: Load the Rate/Rule Schedule with the filed rate tables
actions: Open the Rate/Rule Schedule tab and add one item per rate document, entering the document name, the rate action (new, revised, replacement), the previous state filing number where the item replaces prior rates, and the affected form numbers.
Attach the certified rate tables by plan id and rating area in the format the state prescribes.
Enter the rate change percentages the state requires at the schedule level: overall requested change, minimum, maximum and the number of policyholders affected.
Confirm the attached rate tables carry the frozen package version number in their file names.
checklist.done: the Rate/Rule Schedule lists every rate document with its action, prior filing reference and rate change percentages.

checklist.step: Map the certified package onto the Supporting Documentation schedule
actions: Open the Supporting Documentation tab and satisfy every state-required item: actuarial memorandum, Unified Rate Review Template, actuarial value calculator output, rate change exhibits, cover letter and any state rate template.
Where an item is genuinely not applicable, use Bypass and enter a substantive reason - a blank bypass reason draws an objection by itself.
Attach the plain-language Part II written description for every subject-to-review product.
Check every attachment opens, is text-searchable and is within the SERFF per-attachment size limit before submitting.
checklist.done: no supporting documentation item is left unsatisfied and every bypass carries a substantive reason.

checklist.step: Pay the filing fee and record the payment
actions: Read the fee amount and payment method from the state SERFF Filing Rules page and compare it to the amount on the submission instruction sheet.

Where the state takes EFT through SERFF, complete the EFT screen and record the transaction reference; where the state takes a check, request it from Accounts Payable ahead of the deadline and record the check number and mailing date.
Attach the payment evidence to the filing under the state fee schedule item.
Note the fee amount and reference on the filing tracker row - an unpaid fee stops the review clock in several states.
checklist.done: the fee is paid by the state prescribed method with the reference recorded on the filing and the tracker.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission review before pressing Submit
actions: Open the filing in SERFF and compare it line by line to the submission instruction sheet: company, TOI, effective date, attachment list, rate change percentages, fee.
Confirm the attached memorandum and URRT are the certified frozen versions and carry the signed certification page.
Confirm the requested effective date leaves the state review period intact before the first quoted date.
Record the reviewer name and date on the filing tracker row - the submitter must not be the sole reviewer.
checklist.done: a second named person has reviewed the filing against the instruction sheet and recorded the check.

checklist.step: Submit to the state and capture the SERFF tracking number
actions: Press Submit Filing to State and wait for the submission confirmation rather than assuming it went.
Copy the SERFF tracking number, the state tracking number where the state issues one, and the submission date and time stamp.
Export the Filing at a Glance PDF immediately as the submission receipt and file it in the package folder.
Write the tracking numbers and submission timestamp onto the filing tracker row and the determination log row.
checklist.done: the SERFF tracking number and a dated submission receipt are captured against the filing and the determination log.

checklist.step: Lodge the federal Rate Filing Justification through HIOS
actions: Log in to the CMS Health Insurance Oversight System and open the Unified Rate Review module for the plan year and the issuer id.
Upload the certified URRT for each product and confirm the module validation passes with no blocking errors.
For every subject-to-review product open the Rate Review Justification module and load Part II and Part III against the correct product and market.
Download and file the HIOS submission confirmation for each upload - the confirmation, not the upload screen, is the evidence.
Confirm the URRT lodged federally is byte-identical to the one attached in SERFF.
checklist.done: the federal justification is lodged for every product with a filed confirmation, matching the SERFF attachments.

checklist.step: Register the filing in the tracker with its clocks and owners
actions: Create the tracker row: plan year, state, market, HIOS issuer id, SERFF tracking number, submission date, requested effective date, review method, state review period and the computed decision-expected date.
Set the objection-response service level at the state prescribed response window, or 10 business days where the state sets none.
Name the filing owner, the actuarial responder and the counsel reviewer on the row.
Link the row to the package folder and to the determination log row so an examiner can walk the chain in one hop.
checklist.done: the tracker row carries clocks, owners and links from determination through package to submission.

checklist.step: Monitor SERFF status daily until disposition
actions: Each business day open the SERFF workspace filtered to Status = Submitted to State, Assigned or Pending Industry Response for your states.
Record any status change, objection letter, note to filer or amendment request on the tracker row the same day.
Chase any filing with no state action beyond the state published review period through the SERFF Note to Reviewer function and record the chase.
Escalate to the Regulatory Affairs Manager any filing whose decision-expected date passes without disposition.
checklist.done: every open filing has a status entry no older than one business day and overdue filings are chased and escalated.

checklist.step: Handle amendments and refilings without losing version control
actions: Where the state or CMS requires a rate change after submission, obtain a new certified package version from the Chief Actuary before touching the filing.
Add the revised documents as a new Rate/Rule Schedule item or through the state prescribed amendment path, never by replacing an attachment in place.
Update the rate change percentages, the URRT in HIOS and the Part II text so the state, the federal and the public figures stay identical.
Record the amendment date, the superseded version and the reason on the tracker row.
checklist.done: every amendment is a new certified version, reflected in both SERFF and HIOS, with the superseded version recorded.

checklist.step: Track the federal review and the public posting milestones
actions: Track for each subject-to-review product whether the state runs an effective rate review programme or CMS performs the review, and record which determination applies.
Watch for the CMS public posting of proposed rate increases and confirm the posted figures match the filed average increase for each product.

Where a determination of unreasonableness is issued, convene Pricing, Compliance and Counsel within 2 business days to decide between modification, withdrawal or the public response required under 45 CFR 154.225.
Record every federal milestone and its date on the tracker row.
checklist.done: each subject-to-review product has its federal review track, posted figures checked, and any unreasonableness determination owned.

checklist.step: Capture the disposition and the approval letter
actions: When the state dispositions the filing, open the Disposition tab and read the disposition status, the date and any conditions or approved-as-modified language.
Download the disposition report and the approval letter and confirm the approved rate tables and plan ids are the ones filed, not an earlier version.
Where the disposition is Approved as Modified, extract the modification and route it to the Product / Filing Actuary before anything is implemented.
Record disposition status, disposition date and the approved effective date on the tracker and determination log rows.
checklist.done: the disposition, its date, its conditions and the approval letter are captured and the approved scope is confirmed against what was filed.

checklist.step: Hand the approved earliest-use date to Product Operations
actions: Publish for each state the approved effective date, the approved plan ids and rate tables, and any condition attached to the approval.
Confirm with Product Operations that the release gate for that state can be released only against this record.
Flag states still open so the open enrollment readiness plan shows the true position rather than an assumed approval.
Record the handover date and recipient on the tracker row.
checklist.done: Product Operations holds a per-state approved earliest-use date with conditions, and open states are visibly flagged.

checklist.step: Close the filing record and file the submission evidence
actions: Export the complete SERFF filing - Filing at a Glance, schedules, correspondence and disposition - as the closing record.
File it with the HIOS confirmations and the fee payment evidence in the compliance evidence repository under plan year, state and HIOS issuer id.
Set the tracker row to Closed only when disposition, approval letter and archive link are all present.
Apply the plan-year-plus-7-years retention label to the closing record.
checklist.done: the filing is closed only with disposition, letter and archived export in place, under retention.

testing.step: Build the submission population from SERFF and the determination log
actions: Export from SERFF every health rate filing created for the plan year across all company instances, with tracking number, state, TOI, submission date and disposition.
Join the export to the filing determination log rows flagged filing required, on plan year + state + market.
List determination rows with no SERFF filing and SERFF filings with no determination row as automatic exceptions before sampling.
testing.done: the SERFF export and the determination log are joined with every unmatched row listed as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the federal justification submissions to the population
actions: List every product flagged subject to review in the determination log for the plan year.
Match each to a HIOS Rate Review Justification submission confirmation for Part II and Part III and to a URRT submission confirmation.
Compare the URRT lodged in HIOS to the URRT attached in SERFF for the same product and confirm they are the same version.
Treat a missing federal lodgement or a version mismatch as a fail.
testing.done: every subject-to-review product has matching federal and state submissions of the same certified version.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100 percent of prior approval state filings and 100 percent of filings that were amended or refiled after submission.
Take a seeded random selection of 15 further filings from the remainder, minimum total 30 filings.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratification and the draw date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every prior approval and amended filing.

testing.step: Re-perform the submission completeness check inside SERFF
actions: Open each sampled filing and compare the General Information, Rate/Rule Schedule and Supporting Documentation tabs against the state SERFF Filing Rules requirements for that TOI as they read at the submission date.
Confirm every required supporting documentation item is satisfied or bypassed with a substantive reason.
Confirm the filing company and NAIC co-code match the entity that certified the package.
Capture the Filing at a Glance page into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled filing is confirmed complete against the state requirements in force at submission, with a captured screen.

testing.step: Recompute the submission timeliness against the state deadline
actions: Take the published state initial rate filing deadline for the plan year from the dated filing-rules capture, not from the tracker.
Compare the SERFF submission timestamp to that deadline and compute the days early or late for each sampled filing.
Compare the federal lodgement date to the CMS submission window for the plan year.
Compute the proportion of filings submitted after the state deadline and compare it to the 5 percent escalation threshold.
testing.done: each sampled filing has a computed timeliness result and the late-submission rate is measured against the threshold.

testing.step: Trace the filed attachments back to the certified package version
actions: Open the memorandum and URRT attached in SERFF and read the version number and the certification date on the signature page.
Compare them to the frozen certified version recorded in the document management repository.
Confirm the rate tables attached carry the same version and cover every plan id in the determination row.
Any filing carrying an uncertified or superseded version is a fail regardless of whether the numbers happen to match.
testing.done: every sampled filing carries the certified, current package version across memorandum, URRT and rate tables.

testing.step: Verify the fee payment and the review-clock start
actions: Read the fee amount required on the state filing-rules capture and compare it to the amount paid on the filing.
Trace the EFT reference or check number to the accounts payable record and its clearing date.
Confirm the payment date does not sit after the state acknowledged the filing, where the state ties the review clock to fee receipt.
Log underpayments and late payments as exceptions with the resulting clock impact.
testing.done: each sampled filing has a traced fee payment at the required amount with no clock impact, or the impact is logged.

testing.step: Verify the disposition evidence supports the recorded approval
actions: Open the Disposition tab for each sampled filing and read the status, date and any conditions.
Compare the disposition status and date recorded on the tracker row to what SERFF shows and treat any difference as an exception.
For Approved as Modified dispositions, confirm the modification was routed to the actuary and reflected in a new certified version before implementation.
Confirm the approval letter is archived and names the plan ids and rate tables that were filed.
testing.done: recorded dispositions agree with SERFF, conditions are traced through to a certified change, and letters are archived.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying plan year, state, SERFF tracking number and the defect found.
Assign a root cause - missed deadline, incomplete supporting documentation, wrong entity, unpaid fee, federal lodgement missed, tracker not updated - and an owner.
For any required filing never submitted, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and set the cure date before the first affected effective date where that is still possible.
Carry open exceptions into the next cycle test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where a filing was missed, a counsel-owned self-report assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the submission test
actions: Compute the exception rate and the late-submission rate and compare both to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the SERFF export, the HIOS confirmations and the timeliness recomputation.
Have the independent reviewer, who submitted none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under the plan year in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate, late-submission rate and reporting date exists in the repository.
